bib.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
bib.venue: Communications of the ACM (reprint of NeurIPS 2012); the PDF text is the 2012 NeurIPS layout

question: Can a large, deep convolutional network trained end to end on GPUs with supervised learning classify ImageNet far better than hand-engineered pipelines?
hypothesis: Larger/deeper CNNs, with enough labelled data and techniques against overfitting, keep improving with faster GPUs and bigger datasets.
contributions: One of the largest CNNs to date, best results reported on ILSVRC-2010 and ILSVRC-2012
Highly optimized GPU implementation of 2D convolution and training ops, released publicly
Novel features (ReLU, two-GPU split, local response normalization, overlapping pooling) that improve performance and cut training time

method.summary: Eight-layer CNN (5 conv, 3 fully connected, 1000-way softmax) with ReLUs, local response normalization, overlapping max-pooling, trained by SGD with momentum on two GTX 580 GPUs; dropout in the first two FC layers and two forms of data augmentation limit overfitting.

datasets.name: ILSVRC-2010
datasets.size: ~1.2M train, 50,000 val, 150,000 test images; ~1000 images in each of 1000 categories
datasets.source: ImageNet subset; labelled via Amazon Mechanical Turk
datasets.preprocessing: Rescale shorter side to 256, centre-crop 256x256, subtract training-set mean per pixel; random 224x224 crops + horizontal flips; PCA RGB colour jitter (alpha sd 0.1)

datasets.name: ILSVRC-2012
datasets.size: same sizes as ILSVRC-2010 (1.2M train, 50,000 val, 150,000 test)
datasets.split: test labels not public; val and test error used interchangeably (differ by under 0.1%)

models.name: AlexNet CNN
models.architecture: 5 conv + 3 FC layers, ReLU everywhere, LRN after conv1/conv2, overlapping max-pool (s=2,z=3) after LRN and conv5, 1000-way softmax; split across 2 GPUs

training.objective: multinomial logistic regression (maximize mean log-probability of the correct label)
training.lr_schedule: divide by 10 when validation error stops improving; reduced three times before termination (manual)
training.epochs: roughly 90 cycles through the training set
training.dropout: p=0.5 on the first two fully-connected layers; test time use all neurons with outputs x0.5
training.regularisation: dropout, weight decay, data augmentation (random crops/flips: 2048x set; PCA colour jitter)

other.init: weights zero-mean Gaussian sd 0.01; biases 1 in conv2, conv4, conv5 and FC hidden layers, 0 elsewhere
other.dropout_cost: roughly doubles iterations required to converge

inference.samples: Test: 10 patches (4 corners + centre, plus flips), softmax outputs averaged

other.ensembles: 5 CNNs averaged; 7 CNNs (5 + 2 pretrained on Fall 2011) averaged

metrics.name: top-1 error
metrics.definition: fraction of test images whose correct label is not the model's top prediction

metrics.name: top-5 error
metrics.definition: fraction of test images for which the correct label is not among the five labels considered most probable

eval.protocol: Single runs; no seeds or significance tests reported; ILSVRC-2012 val/test used interchangeably

availability.code: http://code.google.com/p/cuda-convnet/ (GPU conv code and parameter files)

limits: No ablation table for dropout or ReLU on ImageNet itself: ReLU speed claim is on CIFAR-10 with a 4-layer net; dropout benefit is stated qualitatively ('substantial overfitting' without it) with no number.
Hyperparameters were hand-tuned (LR schedule manual, LRN constants on validation); single runs, no seeds or variance.
Authors expect unsupervised pre-training would help; not tested.
Tied to 2012 hardware (3GB GPUs, model split across two); the two-GPU comparison is biased toward the one-GPU net.
Dated: LRN and the two-GPU column split later dropped; dropout 'recently-introduced' (cited as 2012 arXiv).
